chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 307 – The Stomach Rupture: Li Huowang’s Restraint Fails
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang’s attempt to avoid bloodshed leads to a brutal ambush in the reed marsh. When the Black Tai Sui is injured, his grip on reality snaps—and he finds himself eating a rotten orange in a modern downpour.
og_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 307 – The Stomach Rupture
og_description: Li Huowang’s restraint costs him his hand. Pinned by Bai family spears, his hallucination-suppressing parasite dies, and he crashes into modern reality clutching a rotten orange.
twitter_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 307 – The Stomach Rupture
twitter_description: Even trying to be kind, Li Huowang gets his hand cut off. When the Black Tai Sui dies, so does his only anchor to sanity. A brutal gut-punch of a chapter.

lore_anchors.definition: A summoned servant-entity used in Daoist folk sorcery for reconnaissance and gathering; it tracks by blood and can be repelled by the Coin Sword. It has no will of its own, only its master’s orders.
A parasitic entity that suppresses Li Huowang’s hallucinations when it is unharmed inside his stomach; once damaged, the hallucinatory barrier collapses, sending him back to modern reality.
A Daoist ritual weapon made of coins strung on red cord; can be scattered mid-combat to strike multiple supernatural targets at once.
The clan head of the Bai family from Niuxin Village; his earlier warmth turned to cold silence the moment he saw Li Huowang’s Office token.
